bounds: One admitted owner-private text document, three exact text values (leading/trailing newlines, tabs/CRLF, and non-ASCII text), one owner, one detail read, zero or one unchanged save, and one reread. The six model-generated terminal outcomes are replayed through the production routes and PGlite DocumentService.
limitations: This is the document-detail text projection and unchanged-save contract, not the full document lifecycle. Upload authorization, foreign callers, binary records, source segments, concurrent edits, transport cancellation, failed storage, and delivery are outside this model. Existing route and document-service tests own those paths.
An editor discard means no PATCH is sent; it does not claim that an in-flight write can be canceled. Source strings are finite examples, not a proof for arbitrary Unicode text.
Progress assumes the admitted route and storage calls complete. No wall-clock bound, scheduler fairness, provider success, or general implementation refinement is proved.

assumptions: Weak fairness of read, finish and reread: the owner eventually saves or closes the editor, and each admitted route/storage call completes. External I/O completion is abstracted into the transition; safety is unconditional.
